# Current essays: additive-normality revision

29 October 2026. This edition replaces A4 version 4 with version 5 and leaves the accuracy and free-evidence manuscripts unchanged.

| Essay | Version | Words excluding bibliography | Position |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Holistic Accuracy and the Lockean Thesis | A5 v3 | 4,937 | Primary candidate |
| When Acting on Knowledge Makes Free Evidence Harmful | A6 v3 | 5,818 | Primary candidate |
| Limits of Uniform Normality Filters in Actual Causation | A4 v5 | 5,876 | Reserve; strengthened result, further comparison open |

The new A4 Theorem 3 proves that a uniform additive normality score under modified HP cannot preserve the chain and ducking judgments while rejecting the singleton switch cause in the specified binary Doorbells model. Its proof covers all real category scores. An explicit counterexample shows that the obstruction does not extend to original and updated HP. The essay also gives an exact condition for an escape using unequal root weights.

Read [the companion result](additive/Additive-Normality-Obstruction.md) for the full calculation, boundary verdicts, reproduction instructions and originality assessment. [The earlier Halpern comparison](Halpern-Originality-Review.md) remains a dated assessment of version 4; its attribution findings carry forward, while the additive theorem is new to version 5.

The latest source check revisited Dorst's section 4.2 and Proposition 5 proof (193–195, 207), Salow's conditional-dominance discussion, and Hong's 2026 *Normality in Action?*. A5 already makes its final-state reading of Sequence-Irrelevance explicit; a stronger procedural interpretation remains a substantive objection, not a new proof failure. A6 already distinguishes its expected-utility rule from Salow's qualitative principle and credits Hong's prior objections. These targeted comparisons did not identify a concrete reason to revise either primary manuscript. Their earlier numerical checks were not rerun.

No newer Claude draft or review was present after the book-review commit when this edition was prepared. This report records the revising assistant's source comparison and mathematical self-review.

The combined reading copy contains only the three essays. For a contest entry, use an individual anonymous essay and its matching methodology report from the downloadable edition. The combined copy and supplementary note are review material. No contest form has been submitted. E3 remains withdrawn.

The GitHub edition excludes the detailed production-history reports and complete archive, following the earlier automatic approval rejection of those disclosures. They remain in the owner's downloadable edition. The public snapshot contains the essays, scientific companion note and its code/results, the dated source assessment, and a concise index.

One source request remains: the full PDF of Xiao and Xiong, “A refinement of the Hitchcock definition of actual causation” (2026), DOI [10.1057/s41599-026-07470-y](https://doi.org/10.1057/s41599-026-07470-y). Its core definitions and proofs have not been reliably accessed.
